what:
**Web + docs content review feedback (user 2026-04-28 — applies to all launch surfaces):**

The current website + docs prose are too thin and miss the actual aide-memory value prop. Apply across HomePage, all docs pages, and roll the same lens into demo + blog.

**Value-prop framing (this is the big miss):**
- Don't just say "agents have memory loss" — that's the gap-meeting framing. The REAL problems aide-memory solves:
  - Static rules files (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules) get stale, miss context, manual to update
  - Lack of LAYERED memories (preferences vs technical vs area vs guidelines)
  - Lack of TEAM sharing — every dev's agent must rebuild same domain knowledge
  - "Works on my agent" — same problem class as Docker's "works on my machine"
  - Don't capture all context in an area; not always updated; can drift
  - No automatic prompting for recall; agents don't know what context exists
  - Editor/tool lock-in — what you teach Claude Code doesn't carry to Cursor
  - Lack of domain knowledge / org-context portability
- TEAM is a first-class story, not a footnote. Mention "good for individuals AND great for teams" throughout.
- Framing should make uniqueness clear quickly: layered + scoped + auto-capture + git-synced + cross-tool. Surface the differentiation against rules files / skills / standalone memory tools at the top of any explainer.
- "aide-memory uses your existing agent in your existing tools, no extra LLM cost" — mention this, it's a real differentiator.

**Tagline / hero (HomePage.jsx):**
- "MCP-native · Local-first · Zero config" — drop "Zero config" (we have config; honest framing: "Zero config to start" or just remove). Tagline overall not great — workshop a better one.
- HomePage hero color should match the aide-memory CLI brand chrome color (check src/memory/* for brand chrome — looks like the `aide-memory · ...` lines have a specific tint).
- "Persistent, path-scoped memory for AI coding agents. Works across sessions. Works across tools." — must include teams.
- Cards at bottom can be better; less spacing between cards and main; overall polish pass.
- Cross-tool card can drop "five gaps tracked" framing, just say "Claude Code + Cursor today, more editors tracked."
- Telemetry card: be honest about what's sent, opt-in/out story, don't oversell.
- "Structured layers" card should mention personal/shared split.
- "~20 token nudge" — caveat with `~`, or drop the precise number.
- No copy-feedback on the hero install command (clipboard).
- "Get started in 2 min" — is it really 2 min or seconds?

**Overview / docs/index page:**
- "AI coding agents have a memory problem" framing isn't enough. Use the full problem catalog above.
- "How AIDE Memory Works" needs the structural value props, not just hook list:
  - Hooks prompt agent for corrections, important mems, recall when mems exist
  - Injection on new sessions for important stuff
  - Session-scoped tracking (only blocks once per file per session)
  - Recall is path-scoped + layered + auto-prioritized
- Last-updated date should reflect reality.
- "Free. Local-only. No account required." — keep, but reword 2-min claim.

**Concepts page (overlap with Features):**
- I repeated points across concepts and features — consolidate. Each page should have a clearly-different audience or angle.
- Layer examples are too generic ("composition over inheritance", "WAL mode required", etc.) — use richer real-world examples.
- Mention rules files (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules) on Concepts — what they are, where they fall short, how aide-memory complements.
- Scope examples should mention the configurability dial (recall.minScopeDepth) without going deep.
- "Non-goals" section — rename to something better, and at the TOP make it clear what makes aide-memory different from other mem tools, rules files, skills, agents, ads etc — the differentiator headline.
- aide-memory-utilizes-existing-agent line.

**MCP tools page + CLI page:**
- Could be combined into one page (mcp + CLI reference) or at least cross-linked tightly.
- aide_recall purpose: more sophisticated than "fetch memories scoped to paths" — include the scoring/layering/diversity logic at a high level.
- Schema cost claim "~1,400 tokens" — verify, don't guess.

**Hooks page:**
- "Re-block in PostToolUse" — change wording to "re-prompt".
- Stop hook description: it's PERIODIC based on config (every 3 turns ramping to 5 then 10 based on session size). Configurable via `hooks.stop.schedule`.
- PreCompact: I claimed "extracts decisions before compacted away" — verify; pre-compact-save.sh actually clears tracking files + prompts agent to save important context, doesn't auto-extract.
- PreToolUse: clarify configurable (soft vs block). Use "reprompted" / "blocked" language consistently. Be explicit: "prompts when items not recalled for a session, until related mems for scope recalled, blocks when files encountered for first time in session, all configurable."
- Per-editor differences mentioned briefly but defer detail to per-editor pages.

**Configuration page:**
- DROP the "removed in 0.4.3" note. We are FIRST PUBLIC RELEASE, no need to talk about prior versions or migration paths.
- Full config schema in the JSON snippet should INCLUDE every public knob, not just a handful — verify against scripts/hooks/defaults.json.
- `hooks.read.maxBlocks=0` — does NOT fully disable the hook; it just doesn't hard-block (still soft-nudges?). Verify behavior in handlers.ts and rewrite.
- `hooks.search.mode` — does it actually accept "block"? Verify.
- PreCompact mode "cleanup" / "off" — clarify the why: clears recalled-paths so post-compact reads re-prompt cleanly.
- Type column: use `|` not `/` for union shapes (e.g. `boolean | "all"`).
- For `injection.preferences: 15` (and other top-N keys): make explicit it's "top 15 by recall_count desc, updated_at desc".
- recall.minScopeDepth: clearer doc on "when opening a file, what scopes are warranted as relevant per-file vs. SessionStart-only".
- For higher softening threshold, can call out "harder block".
- Add a caveat that the default config aims to capture the normal case but the unique strength of aide-memory is configurability; if you don't want one piece of the flow, you can flip one knob.
- Setting config: mention you can also edit `.aide/config.json` directly (the json is the truth).
- Telemetry: I have stated default off / opt-in. **User now questioning this.** Memory #373 said decision was opt-in default. CONFIRM THE INTENT before doing anything; if it stays opt-in, mention what's sent (event type, hashed machine id, platform, Node version) and how to opt out.
- API key in the bundle: PostHog key is present in dist/cli/aide-memory.js. User flagged this — is it OK that it ships in bundle for opt-in usage? (PostHog write keys are designed to be public; common practice. But verify and explain in docs.)
- "Update checks" — does that config actually work? Verify.
- "Resetting config" guidance: `rm .aide/config.json && aide-memory init` — verify init handles the reset cleanly without clobbering memories.

**Honesty on Cursor framing:**
- Stop being "biased" about Cursor — be honest about Claude Code restart-after-init too where applicable.
- Editor-onboarding flows for both editors should call out the same kinds of friction (restart, MCP enable) where they apply. Don't soft-pedal Claude Code while listing every Cursor friction.

**Process meta-feedback:**
- Several earlier-fixed points regressed in the new MDX (e.g. Cursor parity language in places, hook count). Track at pattern level, not instance level (memory #378 #6).
- "First public release" framing should drive every doc — no "removed in X.Y.Z" backwards-compat language anywhere user-facing.
- The website + docs got ported but not deeply content-reviewed; same applies to any agent-spawned content writing.

**Verification before claiming fixes:**
- Per memory #378: do `cd aide-memory-web && npm run build`, check live deploy, verify each fact against source code (handlers.ts, defaults.json, store.ts), AND read the rendered page rather than just the .mdx.

This memory is the durable summary; specific code-level verifications go into separate technical memories as I land them.
why: User reviewed live website at aide-memory.dev plus docs/overview through configuration page after the docs port and wrote a long structured critique 2026-04-28. The critique: the porting was too mechanical, the value-prop framing is too narrow (only "memory loss"), team story is missing throughout, several factual claims are unverified (telemetry default, schema cost, recall priority order, hooks.search.mode block availability, hooks.read.maxBlocks=0 behavior, PreCompact actual behavior, sub-millisecond claim), examples are generic, "removed in 0.4.3" backwards-compat noise doesn't belong in first-public-release docs, Cursor framing has bias creep back. Without storing this as a guideline, future content-port + content-review work will repeat the same misses and the user will burn another audit cycle to point them out. Marked priority:always so it injects on every doc/launch-content session going forward.
